earnings_transcript_summary: Apple reported Q1 FY2026 (Dec quarter) revenue of $124.3B, up 4% YoY, slightly above consensus. iPhone revenue was $69.1B, up 2% YoY — Apple Intelligence features drove modest upgrade cycle acceleration but below initial hype expectations. Services revenue hit $26.3B, up 14% YoY, the clear growth engine. Wearables were flat. Greater China revenue declined 2% YoY on competitive pressure from Huawei. Gross margin was 46.9%, up 50bps YoY. Tim Cook emphasized the installed base of 2.35B active devices as 'the foundation for our services flywheel.' Management declined to give specific AI revenue metrics. FY2026 Q2 guidance: revenue $95-98B, roughly flat YoY.

sentiment.news_sentiment_summary: Mixed sentiment. Bulls focus on services growth and AI integration into the ecosystem. Bears highlight slowing iPhone growth, China risks, and stretched valuation for a low-single-digit grower. Apple Intelligence reception has been lukewarm vs. initial expectations. Regulatory pressure in EU (DMA compliance) and US (DOJ antitrust case) ongoing.

macro.macro_summary: Consumer spending resilient but moderating. Strong dollar headwind for international revenue (~60% of total). China consumer sentiment weak. Services revenue benefits from installed base monetization regardless of hardware cycle. Interest rate environment neutral for consumer discretionary.
macro.interest_rate_environment: Rates on hold at 4.5%, stable consumer spending environment
macro.relevant_policy_signals: EU Digital Markets Act requiring App Store changes. DOJ antitrust trial ongoing. India manufacturing expansion accelerating to diversify from China supply chain.
